definition: Ratio of soil loss with a support practice (contouring, strip cropping, terracing) to loss with straight-row up-and-down-slope tillage. P = 1 means no support practice.

how_to_estimate.summary: Default to P = 1 everywhere unless you can map a specific support practice. Where a practice is known, use a slope-dependent value from Wischmeier & Smith (1978) / Renard et al. (1997), or a meta-analytic mean from Xiong et al. (2019). Terraces also change the LS factor (shorter effective slope length) - P alone understates their effect.

methods.name: P = 1 (no practice)
methods.notes: Set all classes to 1 and put land-cover effects entirely in usle_c. FS28 did this.

how_to_choose: P is the noisiest RUSLE factor and the hardest to map. If you cannot delineate where contouring / terracing actually occurs, keep P = 1 and do not try to bury a land-cover signal in it. For BMP or restoration scenarios, prefer to represent the change through usle_c (cover/residue) and, for terraces, through the DEM / LS. Record slope basis and source for any P < 1.

records.caveats: This is what FS28 used for every land-cover class. All management effect went into usle_c.
records.provenance: FS28 masterfile, sheet 'SDR Params', crosswalk table (P factor column = 1, 'a-priori assumption')

records.caveats: Most effective on 2-10% slopes and 30-120 m slope lengths; effectiveness collapses on steeper ground and long slopes.
records.provenance: FS28 masterfile, sheet 'SDR Params', 'Methodological decisions' (P narrative)

cover.management: alternating strips of row crop and sod/close-grown crop on the contour

context.derivation: ~half the contour-only P for the same slope

records.caveats: 0.25-0.35 on 3-8% slopes. Grass buffer strips (cheaper, with riparian co-benefits) reach ~52-59% erosion reduction vs ~65% for formal strip cropping (Rajbanshi & Bhattacharya 2023).
records.provenance: FS28 masterfile, sheet 'SDR Params', 'Methodological decisions' (P narrative)

context.derivation: ~half the strip-cropping P; LS recomputed on inter-terrace spacing
context.study_area: USDA RUSLE handbook; Chen, Wei & Chen 2017 meta-analysis (83 field studies)

records.caveats: P 0.10-0.30 AND LS reduced 50-70% by the shorter effective slope length. Combined P+LS reduction 70-90% on moderate slopes; Chen et al. 2017 report mean runoff -50%, soil loss -67%. Do not represent terraces with P alone.

context.derivation: first global meta-analysis of RUSLE P

records.caveats: Variability of P exceeds that of every other RUSLE factor and depends on implementation quality; treat the +/- as real.

records.caveats: Yang et al. (2003) used P as a second land-cover knob rather than a support-practice map. Only reuse this if you are deliberately following that convention; otherwise keep P = 1 and handle land cover in usle_c.
